# guide


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

The learner looks at a walk step, a concept or a video, and says “I
don’t get alpha bar”. The guide answers on the page, as a teacher does
at a whiteboard. It circles the term, draws an arrow to a label in the
figure, moves the slider of the demo, and speaks one short line for each
step.

This module is the part of the guide that has no web page:

- the **board language**: a closed list of drawing commands, each tied
  to a thing on the page (an *anchor*), and the check of each line of
  the model’s reply;
- the **context**: what the page shows, cleaned and cut to size;
- the **gate**: the tutor answers at once when it is sure, else it looks
  in your vault, else on the web;
- the **guard**: no secret and no personal data leaves the Mac in a
  model call or a web query.

The `guide` block serves it, and `core/board.js` draws it.

Import the helpers. The model layer and ramabana load only on the first
call, so the import stays light.

## The board language

A reply is JSON lines: one object on each line. The host checks each
line alone, so a bad line drops and the rest draws. There are 14
commands. The model never writes HTML, CSS, script or a URL.

Each stroke can have `w`: the word of `say` where it starts.

A `sketch` marks a part of a figure only, so no shape covers the words
of the page. A picture of an idea goes in the side panel. For a formula,
the tutor gives an example from day-to-day life and marks the page’s own
formula.

The side panel is the place for a small concrete example (**Explain**).
The tutor builds it one row in each step, from the real values on the
page: its row names the anchor of the value in `at`. The page circles
the value and draws a curve from it to the row, so the model writes no
circle for it. A process of 3 to 5 steps is a panel with `numbered`
rows, or one `chain` row. A new `panel` line starts the next beat, for
example from the values on the page to the big idea. The side panel is
the one picture of Explain. Show is a rupaka demo.

The first line can be a header:
`{"op":"v","n":1,"sure":0.9,"need":"none"}`. `sure` is how sure the
model is, from 0 to 1. `need` says what it needs to be sure: `none`,
`vault` or `web`.

## Anchors

A stroke names a thing on the page. The page sends a list of anchors,
each with an `id`, a `kind` and its `text`. A formula also has its
`tokens` (the TeX of its parts), a figure has its `labels` (a box for
each label in the image), and the demo has its inputs.

Two ways to write the same TeX must match.
[`norm_tex`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#norm_tex)
takes out the spaces and the braces around one symbol.

### norm_tex

``` python
def norm_tex(
    s:str
)->str:
```

*`s` with no white space, and with no braces around one character or one
command, so `\bar{\alpha}_{t}` is `\bar\alpha_t`.*

Braces and spaces do not change the match:

``` python
test_eq(norm_tex(r'\bar{\alpha}_{t}'), norm_tex(r'\bar\alpha_t'))
test_eq(norm_tex(r'\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}'), r'\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}')   # a group of two symbols keeps its braces
test_ne(norm_tex(r'\alpha_t'), norm_tex(r'\bar\alpha_t'))
```

Words match with no case and with white space made single, as the page
shows them.

input `t`.

### by_id

``` python
def by_id(
    ctx
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*`ctx` with `by`: its anchors by id.*

``` python
DDPM = r'q(\mathbf{x}_t\mid\mathbf{x}_0)=\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_t;\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\mathbf{x}_0,(1-\bar\alpha_t)\mathbf{I})'
ctx = by_id(dict(anchors=[dict(id='passage', kind='passage', text='It admits sampling x_t at an arbitrary timestep t in closed form.'),
                          dict(id='m1', kind='formula', text=DDPM, tokens=[r'\bar\alpha_t', r'\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}', r'\mathbf{x}_0', r'(1-\bar\alpha_t)']),
                          dict(id='figure', kind='figure', text='A right triangle', labels=dict(a=[100, 420, 160, 500], b=[480, 880, 540, 960]))],
                 demo=dict(inputs=dict(t=dict(value=500, min=0, max=1000, label='Step t')), open=False)))
```

Each form finds its anchor, and a wrong name does not:

``` python
test_eq(anchor_why('passage', ctx), '')
test_eq(anchor_why(dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar{\alpha}_t'), ctx), '')
test_eq(anchor_why(dict(a='passage', text='Closed  form'), ctx), '')
test_eq(anchor_why(dict(a='figure', label='a'), ctx), '')
test_eq(anchor_why(dict(a='figure', box=[0, 0, 500, 500]), ctx), '')
assert anchor_why('e7', ctx)                                  # an id that the page did not send
assert anchor_why(dict(a='m1', tex=r'\beta_t'), ctx)          # a token that is not in the formula
assert anchor_why(dict(a='passage', text='open form'), ctx)   # words that are not in the passage
assert anchor_why(dict(a='figure', label='c'), ctx)           # a label that is not in the figure
assert anchor_why(dict(a='figure', box=[500, 0, 100, 10]), ctx)
assert anchor_why(dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t', text='x'), ctx)   # two forms at once
```

## The check of one line

[`check_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#check_line)
gives the reason that a line drops, or `''`. Each string in a line is
checked too: no tag, no script and no link can get in, also as the text
of a label.

A cue of the explainer video is `[t, text]`.
[`cue_at`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#cue_at)
gives the cue that plays at `t` seconds.
[`cue_quote`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#cue_quote)
finds a quote in the cue at `t` or in the cue before or after it. It
gives the start of the cue where the quote begins, and the quote as the
transcript says it. The board seeks the video to that start, so a time
that the model gives a little late still lands on the right cue.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L107"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def cue_quote(
    cues, t:float, quote:str
):
```

*`(start, words)` when `quote` (3 words or more) is word for word in the
cue at `t` with the cue before and after it: the start of the cue where
it begins, and the quote as the transcript says it. Else None.*

### plain_say

``` python
def plain_say(
    say:str
)->str:
```

*The spoken line `say` with no semicolon: each part is a sentence of its
own.*

Good lines pass. The checks drop an unknown op, an unknown key, a link
and markup:

``` python
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t'), w=0), ctx), '')
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='label', at=dict(a='figure', label='a'), text='side a', side='left'), ctx), '')
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='arrow', **{'from': dict(a='m1', pt=[1100, 500]), 'to': dict(a='m1', tex=r'(1-\bar\alpha_t)')}), ctx), '')
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='clear'), ctx), '')
assert check_line(dict(op='script', code='alert(1)'), ctx)
assert check_line(dict(op='circle', at='passage', html='<b>'), ctx)
assert check_line(dict(op='label', at='passage', text='see https://evil.example'), ctx)
assert check_line(dict(op='label', at='passage', text='<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'), ctx)
assert check_line(dict(op='step', say='x' * 161), ctx)
```

A sketch marks a part of a figure, with at most 64 points. A sketch on
another anchor drops: a picture of an idea goes in the side panel.

``` python
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='sketch', at=dict(a='figure', pt=[1050, 0]), pts=[[0, 0], [1000, 1000]]), ctx), '')
assert check_line(dict(op='sketch', at='figure', pts=[[i, i] for i in range(65)]), ctx)
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='sketch', at=dict(a='m1', pt=[1050, 0]), pts=[[0, 0], [1000, 1000]]), ctx), 'a sketch that is not on a figure')
```

A circle, a box, an underline or a label marks a thing on the page. On a
bare point it has no thing under it, so it drops. A point and an arrow
can use a point:

``` python
assert 'bare point' in check_line(dict(op='box', at=dict(a='passage', pt=[-200, 900])), ctx)
assert 'bare point' in check_line(dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='passage', pt=[500, 500])), ctx)
test_eq((check_line(dict(op='point', at=dict(a='passage', pt=[-200, 900])), ctx), check_line(dict(op='box', at=dict(a='passage', box=[0, 0, 500, 500])), ctx)), ('', ''))
```

The side panel: a `panel` line with its title, a `row` of short cells
with an optional `to` and anchor, and a `note`. A number in a cell is
good. A long cell, an empty row or an unknown anchor drops:

``` python
test_eq([check_line(o, ctx) for o in (dict(op='panel', title='tensors and targets', head='Make a question and its answer', cols=['Input', 'Target']),
                                       dict(op='row', cells=['[18]'], to=47, at=dict(a='passage', text='closed form')),
                                       dict(op='row', cells=['Guess', 'Compare', 'Adjust'], chain=True), dict(op='note', text='Both can be tensors.'))], [''] * 4)
for bad in (dict(op='row', cells=[]), dict(op='row', cells=['x' * 25]), dict(op='row', cells=['a'], at='e7'), dict(op='panel', cols=['a', 'b', 'c']),
            dict(op='note', text=''), dict(op='row', cells=['a'], chain='yes')): assert check_line(bad, ctx), bad
```

The demo gate: `demo_set` drops while the learner has not locked in a
prediction, so the board cannot give the result first. After the lock-in
it changes only inputs that the demo has, in their range.

``` python
assert 'gate' in check_line(dict(op='demo_set', set=dict(t=500)), ctx)
open_ctx = by_id({**ctx, 'demo': {**ctx.demo, 'open': True}})
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='demo_set', set=dict(t=500)), open_ctx), '')
assert check_line(dict(op='demo_set', set=dict(beta=1)), open_ctx)
assert check_line(dict(op='demo_set', set=dict(t=5000)), open_ctx)
```

`video_at` quotes the transcript at its time, word for word:

``` python
vctx = by_id({**ctx, 'video': dict(id='abc123def45', cues=[[0, 'Today we add noise.'], [61.5, 'Alpha bar is the share of the signal that is left.'], [70, 'It falls as t grows.']])})
test_eq(check_line(dict(op='video_at', t=63, quote='the share of the signal'), vctx), '')
assert check_line(dict(op='video_at', t=63, quote='the share of the noise'), vctx)
assert check_line(dict(op='video_at', t=63, quote='Alpha bar'), vctx)      # too short to be a quote
assert check_line(dict(op='video_at', t=63, quote='the share of the signal'), ctx)   # no video on the page
```

[`cue_quote`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#cue_quote)
gives the start of the cue that holds the quote, and the words as the
transcript has them:

``` python
cs = vctx.video['cues']
test_eq(cue_quote(cs, 63, 'THE SHARE of the signal'), (61.5, 'the share of the signal'))
test_eq(cue_quote(cs, 71, 'share of the signal'), (61.5, 'share of the signal'))   # the time is late: the cue before holds it
test_eq(cue_quote(cs, 63, 'left. It falls'), (61.5, 'left. It falls'))             # a quote across two cues starts in the first
test_eq(cue_quote(cs, 5, 'the share of the signal'), (61.5, 'the share of the signal'))
assert cue_quote(cs, 200, 'Today we add noise.') is None                           # too far from its time
```

## The whole reply

[`parse_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#parse_board)
reads a reply line by line. Each step keeps at most 6 strokes, and a
board has at most 6 steps. A stroke before the first step drops. Two
dropped lines in a row end the board (`failed`): the steps before them
stay.

A step can quote a source: `src` is the number of the source in
`ctx.sources`, and `quote` must be word for word in its text, with 40 to
600 characters (`research.verbatim`, the gate that research uses). A
quote that fails drops, and the step stays, in the tutor’s words.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L249"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### parse_board

``` python
def parse_board(
    text:str, ctx
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The checked board in the model’s reply `text`: `steps`, `dropped` lines
with why, `sure`, `need` and `failed`.*

A board for “I don’t get alpha bar” on the DDPM formula: three steps,
each with its strokes. The header says that the tutor is sure.

``` python
reply = '\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [
    dict(op='v', n=1, sure=0.9, need='none'),
    dict(op='step', say='This formula adds noise in one jump.'), dict(op='box', at='m1', w=2),
    dict(op='step', say='Alpha bar t is how much of the clean picture is left at step t.'),
    dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t'), w=0), dict(op='label', at=dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t'), text='how much is left', side='above', w=5),
    dict(op='step', say='It starts near one and falls to near zero.'), dict(op='sketch', at=dict(a='figure', pt=[1050, 0]), pts=[[0, 100], [500, 500], [1000, 950]])])
b = parse_board(reply, ctx)
test_eq(len(b.steps), 3)
test_eq([len(s['strokes']) for s in b.steps], [1, 2, 1])
test_eq((b.sure, b.need, b.failed, b.dropped), (0.9, 'none', False, []))
```

A bad line drops alone, and the next line still draws. Two bad lines in
a row end the board:

``` python
b = parse_board('{"op":"step","say":"One."}\n{"op":"circle","at":"e7"}\n{"op":"circle","at":"m1"}', ctx)
test_eq((len(b.steps[0]['strokes']), len(b.dropped), b.failed), (1, 1, False))
b = parse_board('{"op":"step","say":"One."}\nnot json\n{"op":"circle","at":"e7"}\n{"op":"step","say":"Two."}', ctx)
test_eq((len(b.steps), b.failed), (1, True))
```

A step that talks about the board, not the idea, drops with its strokes,
such as an excuse for an earlier offer. It does not end the board:

``` python
meta = '\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [dict(op='step', say='You asked to see it move, but this page has no live demo I can start; my earlier offer was misleading.'),
                                         dict(op='box', at='passage'), dict(op='step', say='Alpha bar t is how much is left.'), dict(op='circle', at='m1')])
b = parse_board(meta, ctx)
test_eq(([s['say'] for s in b.steps], b.steps[0]['strokes'], b.failed), (['Alpha bar t is how much is left.'], [dict(op='circle', at='m1')], False))
test_eq([w for _, w in b.dropped], [META_WHY, 'a stroke of a dropped step'])
test_eq([bool(META.search(s)) for s in ('Sorry, I cannot show that.', 'I apologise for the mix-up.', 'The noise is not misleading here.', 'The last step adds noise.')], [True, True, False, False])
```

A row with `at` draws its own circle, so a circle line on the same thing
drops. A row comes to the page with its cells as text. A semicolon in a
spoken line becomes the end of a sentence:

``` python
both = '\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [dict(op='step', say='Alpha bar sets the mix; noise fills the rest.'), dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='passage', text='closed form')),
                                         dict(op='row', cells=[18], to=47, at=dict(a='passage', text='closed form'))])
b = parse_board(both, ctx)
test_eq((b.steps[0]['say'], b.steps[0]['strokes'], b.dropped), ('Alpha bar sets the mix. Noise fills the rest.', [dict(op='row', cells=['18'], to='47', at=dict(a='passage', text='closed form'))],
                                                               [(-1, 'the row draws its own circle')]))
```

A row of a worked example with the answer in a last cell, and no `to`,
gets its answer after the arrow. A chain stays a chain. A head that
names “four stages” over three rows loses the count:

``` python
b2 = parse_board('\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [dict(op='step', say='Work it out.'), dict(op='panel', head='Repeat these four stages', numbered=True),
    dict(op='row', cells=['1.0 and 1.0', '√0.5 × 1 + √0.5 × 1', '1.414']), dict(op='row', cells=['Guess', 'Compare'], chain=True), dict(op='row', cells=['Update'], to='weights')]), ctx)
rs = [s for s in b2.steps[0]['strokes'] if s['op'] == 'row']
test_eq([(r['cells'], r.get('to')) for r in rs], [(['1.0 and 1.0', '√0.5 × 1 + √0.5 × 1'], '1.414'), (['Guess', 'Compare'], None), (['Update'], 'weights')])
test_eq(b2.steps[0]['strokes'][0]['head'], 'Repeat these stages')
```

Some models put the strokes inside the step. They count as the lines
after it:

``` python
b = parse_board('{"op":"step","say":"One.","strokes":[{"op":"circle","at":"m1"},{"op":"box","at":"m1"}]}', ctx)
test_eq(([s['op'] for s in b.steps[0]['strokes']], b.dropped), (['circle', 'box'], []))
```

At most 6 strokes in a step and 6 steps in a board; a stroke before the
first step drops:

``` python
many = '\n'.join(['{"op":"step","say":"One."}'] + ['{"op":"circle","at":"m1"}'] * 6 + ['{"op":"box","at":"m1"}', '{"op":"step","say":"Two."}'])
b = parse_board(many, ctx)
test_eq(([len(s['strokes']) for s in b.steps], len(b.dropped)), ([6, 0], 1))
test_eq(len(parse_board('\n'.join(['{"op":"step","say":"A step."}'] * 7), ctx).steps), 6)
test_eq(parse_board('{"op":"circle","at":"m1"}\n{"op":"step","say":"One."}', ctx).dropped[0][1], 'a stroke before the first step')
```

A quote stays only when it is word for word in its source:

``` python
qctx = by_id({**ctx, 'sources': [dict(title='DDPM', text='A notable property of the forward process is that it admits sampling x_t at an arbitrary timestep t in closed form.')]})
good = dict(op='step', say='The paper says it.', src=1, quote='it admits sampling x_t at an arbitrary timestep t in closed form')
test_eq(parse_board(json.dumps(good), qctx).steps[0]['quote']['src'], 1)
b = parse_board(json.dumps({**good, 'quote': 'it allows sampling x_t at any timestep t in closed form, fast'}), qctx)
assert 'quote' not in b.steps[0] and b.dropped
```

A `video_at` stroke moves to the start of its cue and gets the link to
that time:

``` python
b = parse_board('\n'.join([json.dumps(dict(op='step', say='The video says it.')), json.dumps(dict(op='video_at', t=66, quote='share of the SIGNAL', w=2))]), vctx)
test_eq(b.steps[0]['strokes'], [dict(op='video_at', t=61.5, quote='share of the signal', link='https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123def45&t=61s', w=2)])
```

A line of more than 600 bytes drops. There is no diagram: a picture of
an idea is a side panel, so a diagram line is an unknown op:

``` python
test_eq(parse_board(json.dumps(dict(op='step', say='Long.')) + '\n' + json.dumps(dict(op='label', at='passage', text='x' * 40, side='left' + ' ' * 700)), ctx).dropped[0][1],
        'not one JSON object of 600 bytes or less')
test_eq([w for _, w in parse_board(json.dumps(dict(op='step', say='A tree.')) + '\n' + json.dumps(dict(op='diagram', nodes=[], edges=[])), ctx).dropped], ['an unknown op'])
```

## The context

The page sends what it shows: its address, the walk step, the concept,
the anchors, the demo, the video, and what the learner showed with the
pointer (the focus), and the thread: the last questions on this page.
[`clean_context`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#clean_context)
keeps only the keys that it knows and cuts the text: at most 40 anchors,
300 characters an anchor and 6000 in all. An anchor id has only letters,
digits and `:_-`. An unknown kind becomes `text`. A `try` anchor is the
last graded try of the open check (see *The learner’s answer*): it keeps
its own fields, each with its own bound (`TRY`). The result is a
[`PageContext`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#pagecontext).
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
cleans each context that is not one, so a raw dict from a host is
cleaned too, even when it has a `by` key.

### What the learner shows

While the learner talks or types the question, they can circle a part
with the mouse, or hold the pointer still on it. The host finds the
gestures and sends them as `focus`: a list of items, the latest first.
Each item has a `kind` (`circle` or `point`), the `anchors` under it
(the best one first), a `box` from 0 to 1000 of its first anchor, and
`t`, the milliseconds from the start of the question. An item can have
`words`: what the learner said or typed near that time.

[`_focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#_focus)
keeps at most 5 good items. It keeps only the anchor ids that the page
sent, and drops an item with none of them, with a bad kind or with a bad
box.

### The thread of a page

A learner who asks “say that more simply” or “why?” after a board means
that board. So the page keeps a short thread in memory, and sends it
with the next question: the last 3 turns on this page, each with the
question
([`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said)), the
lines that its board said
([`says`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#says)) and its
tier (`t`). The page forgets the thread when the page changes, after 10
minutes with no question, or when the learner pushes Start fresh. The
server keeps no thread: each question brings its own.

[`_thread`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#_thread)
keeps the good turns, the oldest first: a question of at most 300
characters, at most 6 lines of at most 160 characters, and a known tier.
A turn with no question or no line drops, and so does a turn with a tag
or a link in a line, which a board never says. At most 1500 characters
stay in all: the oldest turn goes first.

The demo part keeps the inputs (with their value, range and label), the
readouts, and whether the gate is open.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L373"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### clean_context

``` python
def clean_context(
    raw
)->__main__.PageContext:
```

*The page context
[`raw`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/settings.html#raw), with
only known keys, cut to size, and with `by` (its anchors by id).*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L370"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### PageContext

``` python
def PageContext(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*A page context that
[`clean_context`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#clean_context)
made.
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
cleans every other context, also one with a `by` key.*

Unknown keys go, and a bad anchor id goes:

``` python
c = clean_context(dict(page='/walk/x/step/1', onload='x', anchors=[dict(id='passage', kind='passage', text='Some  text.'), dict(id='<b>', text='x')]))
test_eq(([a['id'] for a in c.anchors], c.anchors[0]['text'], 'onload' in c), (['passage'], 'Some text.', False))
```

A raw dict with a `by` key is not a
[`PageContext`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#pagecontext),
so [`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
cleans it. A cleaned context stays the same type:

``` python
test_eq((isinstance(c, PageContext), isinstance(dict(c), PageContext)), (True, False))
```

A circle on the formula and a point on the passage stay, the latest
first. An unknown anchor id goes from its item:

``` python
shown = [dict(kind='circle', box=[100, 50, 400, 900], anchors=['m1', 'e7', 'passage'], t=2100.4, words='why is this  here'),
         dict(kind='point', box=[480, 480, 520, 520], anchors=['passage'], t=800)]
c = clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, focus=shown))
test_eq(c.focus, [dict(kind='circle', box=[100, 50, 400, 900], anchors=['m1', 'passage'], t=2100, words='why is this here'),
                  dict(kind='point', box=[480, 480, 520, 520], anchors=['passage'], t=800)])
```

Bad items drop: an unknown kind, no known anchor, a box that is not four
finite numbers from 0 to 1000, and a box that is not a list:

``` python
bad = [dict(kind='lasso', box=[0, 0, 10, 10], anchors=['m1']), dict(kind='point', box=[0, 0, 10, 10], anchors=['e7']),
       dict(kind='point', box=[0, 0, float('nan'), 10], anchors=['m1']), dict(kind='point', box=[0, 0, 2000, 10], anchors=['m1']),
       dict(kind='point', box='0,0,10,10', anchors=['m1']), dict(kind='point', box=[5, 0, 5, 10], anchors=['m1']),
       dict(kind='point', box=[0, 0, 10, 10], anchors='m1'), 'circle']
test_eq('focus' in clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, focus=bad)), False)
test_eq('focus' in clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, focus='m1')), False)
```

At most 5 items stay, and each keeps at most 4 anchors:

``` python
many = [dict(kind='point', box=[0, 0, 10, 10], anchors=['m1', 'passage', 'figure', 'm1'], t=k) for k in range(8)]
c = clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, focus=many))
test_eq(([f['t'] for f in c.focus], c.focus[0]['anchors']), ([0, 1, 2, 3, 4], ['m1', 'passage', 'figure']))
```

A good thread stays, the oldest first. A long line is cut to 160
characters, and an unknown tier is the tutor:

``` python
th = [dict(said='I do not get alpha bar', says=['Alpha bar is the share that is left.', 'x' * 200], t='tutor'),
      dict(said='why?', says=['Each step keeps a part of the signal.'], t='magic')]
c = clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, thread=th))
test_eq([(t['said'], len(t['says'][1]) if len(t['says']) > 1 else 0, t['t']) for t in c.thread], [('I do not get alpha bar', 160, 'tutor'), ('why?', 0, 'tutor')])
```

A bad thread drops: a thread that is not a list, a turn with no question
or no line, and a line with a tag or a link:

``` python
for bad in ('say it again', dict(said='x'), [dict(said='', says=['a'])], [dict(said='x', says=[])], [dict(said='x', says='a line')],
            [dict(said='x', says=['<script>alert(1)</script>'])], [dict(said='x', says=['see https://example.org'])], [7, None]):
    assert 'thread' not in clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, thread=bad)), bad
```

At most the last 3 turns stay, and at most 1500 characters in all. The
oldest turn goes first:

``` python
many = [dict(said=f'question {k}', says=['a line']) for k in range(5)]
test_eq([t['said'] for t in clean_context(dict(thread=many)).thread], ['question 2', 'question 3', 'question 4'])
big = [dict(said=f'q{k}', says=['y' * 160] * 6) for k in range(3)]
th = clean_context(dict(thread=big)).thread
test_eq(([t['said'] for t in th], sum(map(_size, th)) <= THREAD['total']), (['q2'], True))
```

### The learner’s answer

On a walk step or in a session, the page sends the last graded try of
the check as the anchor `try`: the learner’s answer, the outcome, the
feedback, the Error line, the gaps that the answer points at, the state
of the check and the tries that are left. Each field is cut to its
bound, an unknown state is `open`, and a try with no answer and no
feedback drops:

``` python
TRY_RAW = dict(id='try', kind='try', text='Alpha bar grows with t.', answer='Alpha bar grows with t, because more noise is added.',
               outcome='Not yet', feedback='Look at what each alpha is: a number below one.', error='Alpha bar does not grow: it is a product of numbers below one.',
               gaps=['cumulative product', 'cumulative product', 'noise schedule'], state='open', left=2)
a = clean_context(dict(anchors=[TRY_RAW])).anchors[0]
test_eq((a['kind'], a['gaps'], a['state'], a['left']), ('try', ['cumulative product', 'noise schedule'], 'open', 2))
a = clean_context(dict(anchors=[dict(TRY_RAW, answer='x' * 900, state='odd', left=True, gaps='not a list')])).anchors[0]
test_eq((len(a['answer']), a['state'], 'left' in a, 'gaps' in a), (TRY['answer'], 'open', False, False))
test_eq(clean_context(dict(anchors=[dict(id='try', kind='try', text='x')])).anchors, [])
```

## Labels inside a figure

A figure is an image. Its labels (the “a” and “b” on the sides of a
triangle) are not in the page text. The guide finds them once with a
vision call and keeps their boxes for that figure. It keeps only the
boxes, never the image.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L398"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### figure_labels

``` python
def figure_labels(
    vision, img:bytes, alt:str=''
)->dict | None:
```

*The labels in the figure image `img`, as text to a box from 0 to 1000,
from the reply of `vision(prompt, img, sp)`. None when the* call fails
or its reply is not JSON, so that no one keeps an empty result. A key in
`alt` is masked here;
[`vision_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#vision_ask)
guards the full prompt for the model of its route.

[`FigureCache`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#figurecache)
keeps the boxes in one JSON file, by the SHA-1 of the image bytes. A
figure that changes gets a new key.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L415"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### FigureCache

``` python
def FigureCache(
    path, most:int=500, empty_ttl:float=86400.0
):
```

*The label boxes of each figure, by the SHA-1 of its bytes, in the JSON
file `path`. It keeps at most `most` figures. An empty* result is kept
for `empty_ttl` seconds, and only when some figure in the file has
labels: before that, an empty reply can come from a route that lost the
picture, and the next post must ask again.

An empty result is not kept while no figure has labels. After one figure
has labels, an empty result is kept, but only for `empty_ttl` seconds:

``` python
import tempfile
```

``` python
fc = FigureCache(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'figs.json', empty_ttl=60)
test_eq((fc.put('k1', {}), fc.get('k1')), (False, None))
test_eq((fc.put('k2', {'a': [1, 2, 3, 4]}), fc.put('k1', {}), fc.get('k1'), fc.get('k2')), (True, True, {}, {'a': [1, 2, 3, 4]}))
d = fc._all(); d['k1']['at'] -= 61; fc.path.write_text(json.dumps(d))
test_eq(fc.get('k1'), None)   # too old: the next post asks again
```

The vision call goes through ramabana, on the job `guide_vision`:
`compose` puts the image before the text, and the call runs only when
the routed model takes a picture (`accepts`) and its route sends one
([`keeps_images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#keeps_images)).
[`vision_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#vision_why)
says in one line why the call does not run. The prompt and the system
prompt pass
[`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#guard) for
the model of each route, so a model on this Mac gets the text as it is.
With a test model that has no routing, the call is a plain text call
that passes
[`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#guard) for a
hosted model, so a
[`Fake`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#fake) can answer
it.

rishi’s remote one-shot makes its message only from the parts that are
dicts. So the raw image bytes and the text of `compose` do not get to
the model, and the model answers a prompt with no figure.
[`keeps_images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#keeps_images)
finds this with no model call: it gives the same parts to the message
code of the route and looks for the picture.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L472"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### vision_ask

``` python
def vision_ask(
    ask, name:str='', job:str='guide_vision'
):
```

*A vision call `(prompt, img, sp) -> str` on the ramabana job `job` (on
the model of figure labels, by default the model of hints), or None when
the routed model gets no picture
([`vision_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#vision_why)).*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L459"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### vision_why

``` python
def vision_why(
    ask, name:str=''
)->str:
```

*Why the routed model of figure labels (`name`, else the model of
`guide_vision`) gets no picture, or ’’ when it gets one. A test model
with no routing gets one.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L449"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### keeps_images

``` python
def keeps_images(
    spec
)->bool:
```

*Whether the one-shot of the route `spec` sends the picture that
`compose` puts in its prompt. Only rishi’s remote routes are checked; a
check that fails counts as yes.*

## The guard

Text that leaves the Mac passes ramabana’s guard (`ramabana.guard`)
first. `guard(s, model)` is for a model call: the page context and the
question, and the prompt of a vision call. It is `outgoing` for the
model of the route. It always masks API keys, tokens and private keys as
`[SECRET]`. For personal data it follows ramabana’s setting `cli.pii`,
but only for a hosted model: `redact` masks it, `refuse` withholds the
text
([`Withheld`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#withheld)),
and `off` lets it through. A model on this Mac gets the personal data.
When the route is not known,
[`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#guard) takes
a hosted model (`HOSTED`).

`safe_query(q)` is for a web query. It is ramabana’s `query`: a query
with a secret or with personal data does not go, with any setting.

The guard reads text only. A figure image goes to the vision model as it
is: no text guard can read pixels.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L502"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### guarded

``` python
def guarded(
    p, sp, b
)->tuple:
```

*The `prepare` of a routed call: the prompt `p` and the system prompt
`sp` through
[`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#guard) for
the model of the backend `b`.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L496"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### safe_query

``` python
def safe_query(
    q:str
)->str:
```

*The web query `q` as it is, through ramabana’s `query`;
[`Withheld`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#withheld)
when it holds a secret or personal data.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L487"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### guard

``` python
def guard(
    s, model:NoneType=None, mode:str=None
)->str:
```

*`s` as it may go to `model` (a ramabana `ModelSpec`; default `HOSTED`),
through ramabana’s `outgoing`, with the PII policy `mode` (default
`cli.pii`).*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L484"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Withheld

``` python
def Withheld(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*The guard withheld the text: it holds personal data and ramabana’s
`cli.pii` is `refuse`, or it is a web query with a secret or personal
data.*

A key never gets through. Plain text stays as it is:

``` python
test_eq(guard('key sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ here'), 'key [SECRET] here')
test_eq(guard(r'The share \bar\alpha_t is left.'), r'The share \bar\alpha_t is left.')
```

With `redact`, a hosted model gets `[EMAIL]`, and a model on this Mac
gets the address. A key is masked for both:

``` python
local = AttrDict(name='mlx/gemma', local=True)
test_eq(guard('mail ada@example.com', mode='redact'), 'mail [EMAIL]')
test_eq(guard('mail ada@example.com sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ', local, 'redact'), 'mail ada@example.com [SECRET]')
```

With `refuse`, text with personal data for a hosted model is withheld. A
web query with a secret or personal data never goes:

``` python
test_fail(lambda: guard('mail ada@example.com', mode='refuse'), exc=Withheld)
test_fail(lambda: safe_query('alpha bar sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ'), exc=Withheld)
test_fail(lambda: safe_query('alpha bar ada@example.com'), exc=Withheld)
test_eq(safe_query('alpha bar diffusion'), 'alpha bar diffusion')
```

The system prompts of the guide hold no personal data, so `refuse` lets
them go:

``` python
test_eq(guard(prompt('guide.figure'), mode='refuse'), prompt('guide.figure'))
```

A vision reply that a test model gives:

``` python
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
```

``` python
f = Fake({'You find the text labels': dict(labels=[dict(text='a', box=[90, 400, 160, 500])])})
test_eq(figure_labels(vision_ask(f), b'\x89PNG', 'A right triangle'), {'a': [90, 400, 160, 500]})
```

A vision call that fails gives None, not an empty result. The caller
then does not keep it, and asks again the next time.

``` python
def down(p, img, sp=''): raise TimeoutError('the model timed out')
test_eq(figure_labels(down, b'\x89PNG'), None)
```

A route whose message code drops the picture does not keep images. A
route that makes the parts into a picture keeps them. A route of another
kind is not checked:

``` python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from rishi.remote import RemoteChat, to_msg
from urai import mk_msg
```

``` python
cloud, real = SimpleNamespace(runtime='remote'), RemoteChat._oneshot_args
try:
    RemoteChat._oneshot_args = lambda self, p, sp, n: ([to_msg({'role': 'user', 'content': p})], {})
    test_eq(keeps_images(cloud), False)
    RemoteChat._oneshot_args = lambda self, p, sp, n: ([to_msg(mk_msg(p))], {})
    test_eq(keeps_images(cloud), True)
finally: RemoteChat._oneshot_args = real
test_eq(keeps_images(SimpleNamespace(runtime='claude')), True)
```

[`figure_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#figure_check)
is the test of the Settings row *Figure labels*: it sends a picture with
known labels and says which labels came back.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L509"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### figure_check

``` python
def figure_check(
    vision, img:bytes, want:tuple=('Encoder', 'Decoder')
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Whether `vision` reads each label of `want` in the picture `img`: `ok`,
the labels that it `got`, and the `missing` ones. Raise when the reply
is not JSON.*

A reply with both labels passes. An empty reply fails, and names the
missing labels:

``` python
both = json.dumps(dict(labels=[dict(text='encoder', box=[50, 290, 420, 710]), dict(text='Decoder', box=[580, 290, 950, 710])]))
test_eq(figure_check(lambda p, img, sp='': both, b'\x89PNG').ok, True)
test_eq(figure_check(lambda p, img, sp='': '{"labels": []}', b'\x89PNG'), dict(ok=False, got=[], missing=['Encoder', 'Decoder']))
```

## The prompt

The system text says the rules of the board. The parts that change (the
question, the page, the sources) come last in the request, so a
provider’s prompt cache can keep the system text.

Step 1 marks the asked part with a circle or a box, and has at most one
point for context. So a point never takes the place of the main mark.

``` python
test_eq(('mark the part that the learner asked about with a circle or a box' in GUIDE_SP, 'at most one point in step 1' in GUIDE_SP,
         'Point at them when you name them' in GUIDE_SP), (True, True, False))
```

A sketch is for a figure only, and a picture of an idea goes in the side
panel. A question about the answer gets the three steps, and the final
answer waits while tries are left:

``` python
test_eq(('only on a figure anchor' in GUIDE_SP, 'Never use sketch for a picture of an idea' in GUIDE_SP, 'diagram' in GUIDE_SP), (True, True, False))
test_eq(('Step 1 names the problem in their answer' in GUIDE_SP, 'stop before the final answer' in GUIDE_SP,
         'give the full worked solution' in GUIDE_SP, 'up to 4 when the learner asks about their answer' in GUIDE_SP), (True, True, True, True))
ex = [json.loads(l) for l in GUIDE_SP.split('An example reply', 1)[1].splitlines() if l.startswith('{')]
test_eq([check_line(o, ctx) for o in ex if o['op'] != 'v' and o.get('at', {}).get('a') not in ('m1', 'o1')], [''] * 8)
```

A formula gets a day-to-day example in the spoken lines. Each line is
one short sentence, and a code name is said as words:

``` python
test_eq(('day-to-day example' in GUIDE_SP, 'thrown ball' in GUIDE_SP, 'no semicolons' in GUIDE_SP, 'at most 20 words' in GUIDE_SP, 'Say a code name as words' in GUIDE_SP, len(GUIDE_SP) < 6600), (True,) * 6)
```

A process is a side panel with numbered rows. The answer of a row is in
`to`, and a head names no count:

``` python
test_eq(('"numbered":true' in GUIDE_SP, 'the answer in "to"' in GUIDE_SP, 'no number in it' in GUIDE_SP), (True, True, True))
```

The side-panel example passes the check on a page with its output `o1`.
Each row names the words of `o1` that it comes from, and no circle line
repeats them:

``` python
octx = by_id(dict(anchors=[dict(id='o1', kind='text', text='when input is tensor([18]) the target: 47 when input is tensor([18, 47]) the target: 56')]))
pe = [json.loads(l) for l in GUIDE_SP.split('An example side panel', 1)[1].splitlines() if l.startswith('{')]
test_eq([check_line(o, octx) for o in pe], [''] * len(pe))
pb = parse_board('\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in pe), octx)
test_eq([[s['op'] for s in st['strokes']] for st in pb.steps], [['panel', 'row'], ['row'], ['row', 'note']])
```

The prompt says that “show me” works on any page, that code runs in
Leela, and that the tutor never talks about its own board:

``` python
test_eq(('show me on any page' in GUIDE_SP, 'Code that runs is in Leela' in GUIDE_SP, 'Never apologise' in GUIDE_SP), (True, True, True))
```

[`focus_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#focus_text)
tells the model what the learner showed with the pointer, the latest
first, with the words near that time. Step 1 must explain the first
item. The model can mark it with the box of the item, in the anchor form
`{"a": id, "box": box}`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L556"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### focus_text

``` python

    ctx
)->str:
```

*What the learner showed with the pointer, as lines for the request, or
’’ when they showed nothing.*

[`thread_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#thread_text)
gives the earlier turns of the page to the model, the oldest first: each
question and the lines that its board said. The turns are in a fence, so
the model reads them as material, not as instructions. A rule follows:
the new question can refer to them, the board answers the new question,
and it does not give a board again that the learner saw, unless they ask
for it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L574"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

```

*The earlier turns on this page in a fence, the oldest first, with the
rule for them; ’’ when there are none.*

[`page_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#page_text)
writes the anchors as lines for the model: each id, its kind and its
text, with the tokens of a formula, the labels of a figure and the range
of an input. A `try` anchor gives its fields on their own lines, and
says whether the check is open and how many tries are left.

### try_text

```

*The `try` anchor `a` as lines for the request: the state of the check,

The request names the offer at the end of the last step by the kind of
page: “Open it in Leela” on a notebook step, “show me” on the page of an
idea, and none on another page or while a demo is on the page. “Explain
<selection>” of code with numbers asks for the side panel:

``` python
offers = [board_prompt(clean_context(c), 'x').split('\nTier:')[0].rsplit('\n', 1)[1] for c in (dict(slug='noise', leela=True), dict(slug='noise'), dict(page='/settings'))]
test_eq([('Leela' in o, 'show me' in o, 'no offer' in o) for o in offers], [(True, False, False), (False, True, True), (False, False, True)])
withdemo = board_prompt(clean_context(dict(slug='noise', demo=dict(slug='noise-demo', inputs={'t': dict(value=1)}))), 'x')
assert 'Say show me' not in withdemo and 'A demo is on the page' in withdemo   # no Show offer while a demo is on the screen
code = clean_context(dict(slug='noise', anchors=[dict(id='code1', kind='code', text='assert add_noise_loss([1.0, 1.0], [1.0, -1.0], 0.5, [1.0, 1.0]) == ([1.414, 0.0], 2.0)')]))
assert 'Build the side panel from the values' in board_prompt(code, 'Explain "add_noise_loss([1.0, 1.0], [1.0, -1.0], 0.5"')   # a selection of code with numbers
assert 'Build the side panel' not in board_prompt(code, 'Explain "add_noise_loss"') and 'Build the side panel' not in board_prompt(code, 'what is this')
assert 'Build the side panel from the values in the code' in board_prompt(code, 'Work through the third test with its numbers: how do we get 1.414?')   # a typed ask about the values
assert 'Build the side panel' not in board_prompt(clean_context(dict(slug='noise')), 'work through it with its numbers')   # no code with numbers on the page
```

The request names the focused anchors before the page, the latest first,
and says what step 1 must do:

``` python
c = clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, focus=shown))
p = board_prompt(c, "why is this here")
test_eq(p.index('circled m1, passage') < p.index('pointed at passage') < p.index('- passage (passage)'), True)
assert 'near the words "why is this here"' in p and '{"a":"m1","box":[100,50,400,900]}' in p and 'at 2.1 s' in p
```

With no focus, the request is as before:

``` python
test_eq(focus_text(clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors))), '')
assert 'pointer' not in board_prompt(clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors)), 'x')
```

The request has the earlier turns only with a thread. They come after
the page and before the sources, with the rule:

``` python
th = [dict(said="I don't get alpha bar", says=['Alpha bar is the share that is left.'], t='tutor')]
p = board_prompt(clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, thread=th)), 'say that more simply')
test_eq(p.index('<source title="the page">') < p.index('Earlier on this page') < p.index('"Alpha bar is the share that is left."') < p.index('No sources.'), True)
assert THREAD_RULE in p and 'Board (tutor):' in p
assert 'Earlier on this page' not in board_prompt(clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors)), 'x')
```

The try goes into the page part of the request with each of its fields:

``` python
p = board_prompt(clean_context(dict(anchors=[*ctx.anchors, TRY_RAW])), 'explain the gaps')
test_eq(("try (try): the learner's last graded try on the check. The check is open, with 2 tries left." in p,
         '  answer: "Alpha bar grows with t, because more noise is added."' in p, '  gaps: ["cumulative product", "noise schedule"]' in p), (True, True, True))
```

## The explainer video

A concept can have one explainer video from YouTube. The tutor finds one
with fossick’s `search_yt`, or you paste a link. fossick reads the
transcript and its timed cues (`read_yt`). The vault files the
transcript as a document (`Vault.youtube`), and the cues go into its
meta. The concept keeps the video in its provenance as `src='video'`. A
video is a source like any other: a quote from it must be word for word,
and the board names it as *video*, with its channel and title.

abhyasa reads no transcript itself. The id comes from fossick’s
`yt_link`, which refuses a link that names no video.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L653"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

    cues
)->list:
```

*fossick’s cues `{start, end, text}` as the board’s `[start, text]`,
with empty lines dropped.*

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L645"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

```

*The id of a YouTube link or id, as fossick’s `yt_link` reads it. Raise

A link, a short link and a bare id give the same id. Another site does
not:

``` python
for u in ('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123def45&t=3s', 'https://youtu.be/abc123def45', 'abc123def45'): test_eq(video_id(u), 'abc123def45')
test_fail(lambda: video_id('https://example.com/watch?v=abc123def45'))
test_fail(lambda: video_id('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=short'))
test_eq(video_cues([dict(start=1.234, end=3, text=' Hello  there '), dict(start=4, end=5, text='')]), [[1.23, 'Hello there']])
```

[`find_explainer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#find_explainer)
searches YouTube for an idea. The query passes
[`safe_query`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#safe_query),
as each web query that leaves the Mac does. It takes the first result
that is a video of 1 to 60 minutes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L659"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### find_explainer

``` python
def find_explainer(
    name:str, topic:str='', search:NoneType=None, n:int=5

```

*The first video that fossick’s `search_yt` finds for the idea `name`,
as `id`, `title`, `channel` and `url`; None when there is none.*

A fake search: a short clip and a playlist are passed over. A query with
a key does not go, also when the key is after the first 150 characters:

``` python
said = []
def fake_search(q, n): said.append(q); return [dict(id='short000001', duration=20), dict(id='PLlist', title='A list'),
                                                dict(id='abc123def45', title='Alpha bar, simply', channel='Maths Room', duration=600)]
v = find_explainer('alpha bar', 'diffusion', search=fake_search)
test_eq((v.id, v.channel, v.url), ('abc123def45', 'Maths Room', 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123def45'))
test_fail(lambda: find_explainer('alpha bar', 'diffusion sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ', search=fake_search), exc=Withheld)
test_fail(lambda: find_explainer('x' * 180, 'sk-a1B2c3D4e5F6g7H8i9J0k1L2', search=fake_search), exc=Withheld)
test_eq(said, ['alpha bar diffusion explained'])
```

[`file_video`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#file_video)
files the video and makes it the explainer of a concept. `Vault.youtube`
reads the transcript through fossick, and `read_yt` with `cues=True`
then gives the cues from fossick’s cache, with no second fetch. The link
must be public (`allow_private=False`). A concept keeps one video: a new
one takes the place of the old one.

### file_video

``` python
def file_video(
    lr, url:str, slug:str=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*File the YouTube video `url` in the vault with its cues, and make it
the explainer of concept `slug`. Return its provenance entry.*

A test with fakes: fossick’s `read_yt` gives a transcript with three
cues, and the URL check passes. No call leaves the test.

``` python
import fossick.core, abhyasa.sources
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
```

``` python
CUES = [dict(start=0.0, end=4.0, text='Today we add noise.'), dict(start=61.5, end=69.0, text='Alpha bar is the share of the signal that is left.'),
        dict(start=70.0, end=75.0, text='It falls as t grows.')]
def fake_read_yt(url, force=False, cues=False, **kw):
    v = dict(title='Alpha bar, simply', channel='Maths Room', description='A short talk.', duration=600, upload_date='20260101',
             source=' '.join(c['text'] for c in CUES) + f' ({url})')
    return {**v, 'cues': CUES} if cues else v
real = fossick.core.read_yt, abhyasa.sources.public_url
fossick.core.read_yt, abhyasa.sources.public_url = fake_read_yt, lambda u: u
lr = temp_learning()
slug = lr.put('Alpha bar', 'How much of the clean picture is left at step t.').slug
```

Filing links the video to the concept, and the vault keeps the cues:

``` python
e = file_video(lr, 'https://youtu.be/abc123def45', slug)
test_eq((e.src, e.vid, e.channel), ('video', 'abc123def45', 'Maths Room'))
test_eq(concept_video(lr.concept(slug))['doc_id'], e.doc_id)
v = video_of(lr, 'abc123def45')
test_eq((v.title, v.cues[1]), ('Alpha bar, simply', [61.5, 'Alpha bar is the share of the signal that is left.']))
assert 'share of the signal' in lr.vault.shelf(e.shelf).document(e.doc_id).text
test_eq(file_video(lr, 'abc123def45', slug).doc_id, e.doc_id)   # the same link again files nothing new
```

A second video takes the place of the first, and
[`set_video`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#set_video)
with no entry takes it away:

``` python
file_video(lr, 'zzz123def45', slug)
test_eq([p['vid'] for p in lr.concept(slug)['provenance'] if p['src'] == 'video'], ['zzz123def45'])
set_video(lr, slug)
assert concept_video(lr.concept(slug)) is None
fossick.core.read_yt, abhyasa.sources.public_url = real
```

## A board as a hint

On a page with an open check (the anchor `check`), a board counts as one
hint on the check only when it is about the check
([`on_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#on_check)):
the learner showed the check with the pointer, or named it (“check”,
“question”, “answer”, “hint”, “quiz”), or the main words of the question
are words of the check (two of them, or all when there are fewer). The
guide decides this before it asks, so it can tell the learner first. A
board that does not count may not touch the check: the request says so
(`OFF_CHECK`), and a stroke on the check drops. Then the learner keeps
the hints for a real hint.

When the page sends the learner’s last try (the anchor `try`), a
question about the try counts too: one that names the gaps, the try, a
mistake, an error, what is wrong or the feedback (`TRY_ASK`), or a
pointer on the try. Then the request says so (`ON_TRY`), and the model
follows the rule for a question about an answer. A board that does not
count gets no try.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L720"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### on_check

``` python
def on_check(
    ctx, said:str
)->bool:
```

*Whether a board on
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said) counts as
a hint on the open check of `ctx` (the anchor `check`).*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L715"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### asked_words

``` python
def asked_words(
    s:str
)->set:
```

*The main words of `s` (`ground.main_words`) with a light plural stem,
without the words that every question has.*

A page with an open check on the cumulative share alpha bar:

``` python
chk = clean_context(dict(anchors=[*ctx.anchors, dict(id='check', kind='check', text='Why does alpha bar fall toward zero as t grows?')]))
```

A question on the words of the check counts, and so does a question that
names the check. An off-topic question does not:

``` python
test_eq(on_check(chk, "I don't get alpha bar"), True)
test_eq(on_check(chk, 'What does this question want?'), True)
test_eq(on_check(chk, 'Who wrote the Kamba Ramayanam?'), False)
test_eq(on_check(clean_context(dict(anchors=ctx.anchors)), "I don't get alpha bar"), False)   # no open check: never a hint
```

The pointer on the check counts too, whatever the words:

``` python
test_eq(on_check(clean_context(dict(chk, focus=[dict(kind='point', box=[0, 0, 10, 10], anchors=['check'])])), 'what is this'), True)
```

With the learner’s try on the page, “explain the gaps” counts. With no
try, the same words do not:

``` python
tried = clean_context(dict(anchors=[*chk.anchors, TRY_RAW]))
test_eq((on_check(tried, 'explain the gaps'), on_check(chk, 'explain the gaps'), on_check(tried, 'Who wrote the Kamba Ramayanam?')), (True, False, False))
```

## The three tiers

The guide asks in up to three tiers, and the board shows which one it
used:

1.  **tutor**: the page alone. When the model says that it is sure
    (`sure` of `SURE` or more), the board draws at once. The passage on
    the page is source 1, so a quote from it shows as *your source*.
2.  **vault**: else the guide searches your sources
    ([`ground`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/ground.html#ground))
    and asks again with the passages that it finds.
3.  **web**: else, when research is on, it searches the web, reads the
    pages, and takes a passage that is word for word in the page
    (`research.pick_passage`, the gate of research). Then it asks one
    last time with that passage. The page goes into your vault, linked
    to the concept. The page says so at the end of the board, with Undo
    ([`unsave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#unsave)).

When no tier is sure, the best board so far shows, in the tutor’s own
words.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L755"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*The video `v` (from

as a source: its transcript, labelled* video*, with its channel and
title.*

### source_label

``` python
def source_label(
    p
)->str:
```

*The label of passage `p` by its real source:* your vault\* for a vault
shelf, else the label of its source, such as *web*.\*

The guide uses the model that Settings names for the screen guide. With
no model of its own, it uses the model for hints. Here a stand-in for
[`RouteAsk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#routeask)
gives the job and the model of each call.

``` python
from abhyasa.llm import Router
```

``` python
class Via:
    "A stand-in for `RouteAsk`: each `ask` replies with its job and its model."
    model = 'claude/sonnet'
    def via(self, job, name='', cap=None, prepare=None):
        f = lambda p, sp='': f'{job}:{name or self.model}'
        f.model = name or self.model
        return f
test_eq(guide_ask(Router(Via(), models=lambda: dict(hint='claude/haiku')))('hi'), 'guide:claude/haiku')
test_eq(guide_ask(Router(Via(), models=lambda: dict(hint='claude/haiku', guide='claude/opus')))('hi'), 'guide:claude/opus')
test_eq(guide_ask(Router(Via(), models=lambda: {})).model, 'claude/sonnet')
```

## Never caught unaware

The learner must always know what the guide does now, and where the text
goes. So before each step of its work,
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
sends a state event to `on_state`. The guide route sends each one to the
page as it comes, and the page shows it in one line, the guide bar. The
Mac overlay reads the same events. This is the one shape:

``` json
{"wait": "<one STE sentence>", "state": "reading" | "asking" | "searching" | "saving" | "drawing",
 "model": "<model label>", "where": "on this Mac" | "hosted", "who": "<company of a hosted model, or ''>",
 "query": "<the web query word for word, only for searching>", "sources": <count of vault passages or web pages that go to the model>}
```

`wait` is always a full sentence, because an old page reads only `wait`.
A field that does not apply is not in the event.
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
sends `asking`, `searching`, `reading` and `saving`. The page itself
shows `reading` for its own read, and `drawing` when the first step
draws, so the route never sends a line that covers the board.

When the guide files a web page in the vault,
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
sends `{"saved": {...}}` with the document and the concept link. The
route gives the page `{"saved": {"title", "url", "undo"}}`, where `undo`
is the POST route that takes the page and its link away again
([`unsave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#unsave)).

[`where_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#where_of)
(from `abhyasa.llm`) tells who runs a model. It uses the label of
[`model_label`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#model_label)
and the locality of ramabana (`is_local`, which knows the endpoint of an
Ollama model). The model rows in Settings use the same function.

A Claude model is hosted by Anthropic. A model that the guide does not
know counts as hosted:

``` python
test_eq(where_of('claude/sonnet'), dict(model='Claude Sonnet', where='hosted', who='Anthropic'))
test_eq(where_of(''), dict(where='hosted'))
```

A model on this Mac sends nothing off the Mac, and the line says so:

``` python
test_eq(where_of('mlx/gemma-4-e4b-it'), dict(model='Gemma 4 E4B', where='on this Mac', who=''))
test_eq(_asks(where_of('mlx/gemma-4-e4b-it'))['wait'], 'Sends your question and the page text to Gemma 4 E4B. Nothing leaves this Mac.')
test_eq(_asks(where_of('claude/sonnet'), thread=True)['wait'], 'Sends your question, the page text and your last questions on this page to Claude Sonnet.')
test_eq(_asks(where_of('claude/sonnet'), f"Sends {_n(3, 'passage')} from your vault")['wait'], 'Sends 3 passages from your vault to Claude Sonnet.')
```

[`web_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#web_sources)
is tier 3: it searches with a query that passes
[`safe_query`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#safe_query),
reads at most 2 pages, and keeps a passage only when it is word for word
in the page. A query that may not go gives no source. A search that
gives no passage says so in a state event, and
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
asks once more with `NO_WEB` when the best board asked for the web: so
the board does not ask for the web that the guide already searched.
