<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L842"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### unsave

``` python
def unsave(
    lr, s
)->int:
```

*Take back what the guide saved (`s`, from a
[`saved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/prompts.html#saved)
event): the link of the page to the concept, and the page when the guide
added it. The count of changes.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L800"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### web_sources

``` python
def web_sources(
    ask, ctx, said:str, search:NoneType=None, fetch:NoneType=None, lr:NoneType=None, on_state:NoneType=None
)->list:
```

*Sources from the web for
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said), each
with a passage that is word for word in its page. `on_state` gets a
state event before* the search (with the query word for word), before
each read and model call, and before the page goes into the vault. Then
it gets `{"saved": ...}` when the guide added the page or its link to
the concept: what
[`unsave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#unsave)
needs to take them away. When the web gives no passage, a state event
says why (`WEB_FAILED`, `WEB_NO_PAGE`, `WEB_NO_PASSAGE`).

A key after the first 200 characters still stops the query: the guard
reads the whole query before it is cut.

``` python
asked = []
test_eq(web_sources(None, by_id({}), 'x' * 180 + ' sk-a1B2c3D4e5F6g7H8i9J0k1L2', search=lambda q, n: asked.append(q) or []), [])
test_eq(asked, [])
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L857"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### explain

``` python
def explain(
    ask, ctx, said:str, sources:tuple=(), search:NoneType=None, fetch:NoneType=None, web:bool=None,
    note:NoneType=None, lr:NoneType=None, on_step:NoneType=None, stop:NoneType=None, on_state:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The board for
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said) on the
page `ctx`: from the tutor when it is sure, else from your `sources`
(the vault), else from the* web when `web` (default: the setting
`research.on`). `on_state(event)` gets a state event before each step of
the work, and `{"saved": ...}` when a web page goes into the vault (see
*Never caught unaware*); `note(text)` gets only the `wait` line. With a
model that can stream, `on_step(step, k)` gets each step of a sure tutor
board as soon as it is whole
([`stream_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#stream_board)).
When the `threading.Event` `stop` is set, the stream closes and no next
tier starts. `hint` is True when the board counts as a hint on the open
check
([`on_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#on_check));
the first state event says so.

A sure reply draws at once, from one call:

``` python
sure = '\n'.join([json.dumps(dict(op='v', n=1, sure=0.9)), json.dumps(dict(op='step', say='Alpha bar t is the share that is left.')),
                  json.dumps(dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t')))])
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure})
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar")
test_eq((r.tier, len(f.calls), r.end), ('tutor', 1, NO_SOURCE))
```

An unsure reply with research off and no vault stays in the tutor’s
words:

``` python
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.4')})
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", web=False)
test_eq((r.tier, len(f.calls)), ('tutor', 1))
```

Before its one call, the guide says who gets the question. A test model
has no name, so it is “the tutor”, and hosted:

``` python
evs = []
r = explain(Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure}), dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", on_state=evs.append)
test_eq(evs, [dict(wait='Sends your question and the page text to the tutor.', state='asking', where='hosted')])
```

An unsure tutor with research on: the guide looks in the vault, searches
the web with the query word for word, reads one page, files it in the
vault and links it to the concept. Each step has its event first, and
the page that went into the vault comes in
[`saved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/prompts.html#saved):

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
```

``` python
wl = temp_learning(); wl.put('Alpha bar', 'The share of the signal that is left.', 'ml')
text = 'Home. The cumulative product alpha bar t tells how much of the original signal remains after t noising steps.'
pick = dict(passage=text[6:])
webq = '\n'.join([sure.split('\n')[0], json.dumps(dict(op='step', say='A page says what alpha bar t is.', src=1, quote=text[6:]))])
f = Fake({'Tier: web': webq, 'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.3'), 'Return JSON: {"passage"': pick})
evs = []
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, slug='alpha-bar', concept='Alpha bar'), "I don't get alpha bar", lr=wl, web=True, on_state=evs.append,
            search=lambda q, n: [dict(title='DDPM', href='https://example.org/ddpm')], fetch=lambda u: AttrDict(url=u, title='DDPM explained', text=text))
test_eq([e.get('state') or 'saved' for e in evs], ['asking', 'searching', 'reading', 'asking', 'saving', 'saved', 'asking'])
test_eq((evs[1]['wait'], evs[1]['query']), ('Searches the web for: "I don\'t get alpha bar Alpha bar"', "I don't get alpha bar Alpha bar"))
test_eq((evs[2]['wait'], evs[-1]['wait'], evs[-1]['sources']), ('Reads example.org.', 'Sends 1 passage from the web to the tutor.', 1))
s = evs[5]['saved']
test_eq((s['title'], s['url'], s['doc_new'], s['link_new'], r.tier), ('DDPM explained', 'https://example.org/ddpm', True, True, 'web'))
```

[`unsave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#unsave)
takes the link and the page away again:

``` python
test_eq(unsave(wl, s), 2)
test_eq([p for p in wl.concept('alpha-bar').get('provenance') or () if p.get('src') == 'web'], [])
test_eq(unsave(wl, s), 0)   # a second Undo changes nothing
```

The focus that a host sends reaches the model:
[`explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#explain)
cleans the raw context, and the prompt names the circled formula:

``` python
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure})
explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, focus=[dict(kind='circle', box=[0, 0, 500, 1000], anchors=['m1'], t=900)]), "what is this")
assert 'circled m1: box [0, 0, 500, 1000] of m1, at 0.9 s' in f.calls[0][0]
```

A follow-up: “say that more simply” after a board. The host sends the
thread in the raw context, and the prompt gets the lines that the
learner heard. The first state event says that the last questions go
too. The thread passes the guard with the rest of the prompt, so a key
in an earlier question never reaches the model:

``` python
f, evs = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure}), []
th = [dict(said="I don't get alpha bar sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ", says=['Alpha bar t is the share that is left.', 'It falls as t grows.'], t='tutor')]
explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, thread=th), 'say that more simply', on_state=evs.append)
p = f.calls[0][0]
assert '"Alpha bar t is the share that is left." "It falls as t grows."' in p and 'Learner: "say that more simply"' in p
assert 'sk-test1234567890' not in p and '[SECRET]' in p
test_eq(evs[0]['wait'], 'Sends your question, the page text and your last questions on this page to the tutor.')
```

With a video on the page, its cues go into the prompt, and its
transcript is a source. A `video_at` that quotes the cue draws at the
start of that cue, and the end line names the video:

``` python
vid = dict(id='abc123def45', title='Alpha bar, simply', channel='Maths Room', cues=vctx.video['cues'])
reply = '\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [dict(op='v', n=1, sure=0.9), dict(op='step', say='The video says what alpha bar is.'),
                                           dict(op='video_at', t=64, quote='the share of the signal that is left')])
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': reply})
r = explain(f, PageContext(by_id({**ctx, 'video': vid})), "I don't get alpha bar")   # as the guide route: the cues come from the vault, after the clean
assert '[62 s] Alpha bar is the share of the signal that is left.' in f.calls[0][0]
test_eq(r.steps[0]['strokes'][0]['t'], 61.5)
test_eq([(s['label'], s['title'], s['quoted']) for s in r.sources], [('video', 'Maths Room · Alpha bar, simply', True)])
test_eq(r.end, WITH_SOURCE)
```

On the page with the check, a question on the check counts as a hint,
and the first state event says so before the call:

``` python
evs = []
r = explain(Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure}), chk, "I don't get alpha bar", on_state=evs.append)
test_eq((r.hint, evs[0]['hint'], evs[0]['wait'].endswith(COUNTS)), (True, True, True))
```

An off-topic question does not count, the first event says nothing on
hints, the request tells the model to keep off the check, and a stroke
on the check drops:

``` python
evs, mark = [], sure + '\n' + json.dumps(dict(op='box', at='check'))
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': mark})
r = explain(f, chk, 'Who wrote the Kamba Ramayanam?', on_state=evs.append)
test_eq((r.hint, 'hint' in evs[0], OFF_CHECK in f.calls[0][0]), (False, False, True))
test_eq(([s['op'] for s in r.steps[0]['strokes']], r.dropped), (['circle'], 1))
```

“Explain the gaps” with the learner’s try on the page: the request has
the try with its feedback and gaps, and says to follow the rule for an
answer. It counts as one hint. An off-topic question on the same page
sends no try:

``` python
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure})
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=[*chk.anchors, TRY_RAW]), 'explain the gaps')
p = f.calls[0][0]
test_eq((r.hint, ON_TRY in p, 'Alpha bar grows with t, because more noise is added.' in p, 'Look at what each alpha is' in p, 'noise schedule' in p),
        (True, True, True, True, True))
f = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure})
explain(f, dict(anchors=[*chk.anchors, TRY_RAW]), 'Who wrote the Kamba Ramayanam?')
test_eq(('noise schedule' in f.calls[0][0], ON_TRY in f.calls[0][0]), (False, False))
```

The passages from your sources must be on the question. A passage that
names too few of its main words goes to no model, and the guide says
that it found none:

``` python
from abhyasa.ground import passage
```

``` python
class Lib:
    name = 'library'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('library', 'r1', 'Rigveda 05 061 070', 'The Maruts get the gifts of the bar of gold.')])
f, evs = Fake({'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.3')}), []
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors, concept='Diffusion'), "I don't get alpha bar", sources=[Lib()], web=False, on_state=evs.append)
test_eq((len(f.calls), [e['wait'] for e in evs[1:]]), (1, ['Looks in your vault.', 'Found no passage on this in your vault.']))
```

A passage that passes keeps the label of its real source, not *your
vault*:

``` python
class Lib2(Lib):
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('library', 'r2', 'Notes', 'Alpha bar t is the share of the signal that is left.')])
f, evs = Fake({'Tier: vault': sure, 'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.3')}), []
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", sources=[Lib2()], web=False, on_state=evs.append)
test_eq((r.sources[0]['label'], evs[-1]['wait']), ('library', 'Sends 1 passage from library to the tutor.'))
```

The tier and the end line come from what the board quotes. A sure vault
board that quotes nothing is in the tutor’s words, with no source:

``` python
note = 'Alpha bar t is the product of the alphas up to step t, so it falls from one toward zero as t grows.'
class Notes:
    name = 'vault'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('vault:notes', 'n1', 'My DDPM notes', note)])
r = explain(Fake({'Tier: vault': sure, 'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.3')}), dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", sources=[Notes()], web=False)
test_eq((r.tier, r.end, [s['quoted'] for s in r.sources]), ('tutor', NO_SOURCE, [False]))
```

An unsure vault board that quotes the vault is the best board. It keeps
the sources of its own request, so the quoted source is in the list:

``` python
vq = '\n'.join([json.dumps(dict(op='v', n=1, sure=0.5)), json.dumps(dict(op='step', say='Your notes say what alpha bar is.', src=1, quote=note.split(', so')[0]))])
r = explain(Fake({'Tier: vault': vq, 'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.3')}), dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", sources=[Notes()], web=False)
test_eq((r.tier, r.end, [(s['label'], s['quoted']) for s in r.sources]), ('vault', WITH_SOURCE, [('your vault', True)]))
```

When the web pages have no passage, the guide says so. Then it asks once
more, and the request says that the web was searched and gave nothing:

``` python
evs = []
f = Fake({NO_WEB: sure.replace('0.9', '0.5'), 'Tier: tutor': sure.replace('0.9', '0.3').replace('"sure": 0.3', '"sure": 0.3, "need": "web"'), 'Return JSON: {"passage"': dict(passage='')})
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", web=True, on_state=evs.append,
            search=lambda q, n: [dict(title='DDPM', href='https://example.org/ddpm')], fetch=lambda u: AttrDict(url=u, title='DDPM', text='Nothing on it.'))
test_eq(WEB_NO_PASSAGE in [e['wait'] for e in evs], True)
test_eq((len([c for c in f.calls if 'Tier: tutor' in c[0]]), NO_WEB in f.calls[-1][0], r.sure), (2, True, .5))
```

A search with no page says that too:

``` python
evs = []
web_sources(None, by_id({}), 'alpha bar', search=lambda q, n: [], on_state=evs.append)
test_eq(evs[-1]['wait'], WEB_NO_PAGE)
```

## The board as it comes

A board takes some seconds to write. So the tutor tier streams it, and
the first step draws while the model writes the next one.
[`stream_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#stream_board)
reads the reply as it comes. When a new line is in, it reads the whole
lines so far again with
[`parse_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#parse_board),
so the rules are the same as for a whole reply. When the header says
`sure` of `SURE` or more, `on_step(step, k)` gets each step as soon as
its spoken line and its first mark are in, and again each time it gets
more strokes: so the first mark does not wait for the rest of the step
(the rows of a side panel) or for the next step. The page adds the
strokes that it does not have yet. A step that is not sure, or a reply
with no header, sends nothing, and the guide goes on to the vault and
the web as before. The board that
[`stream_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#stream_board)
returns is the truth: its first steps are the steps that went to
`on_step`.

When the stream breaks after a step went out, the board keeps the whole
lines that came, so the page does not lose what it shows.

The learner can stop: a newer question, Esc, or a closed tab. Then the
guide route sets the `threading.Event` `stop`.
[`stream_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#stream_board)
reads no more chunks and closes the stream. So the model call ends at
once, and the next question does not wait for the backend.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/guide.py#L915"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### stream_board

``` python
def stream_board(
    chunks, ctx, on_step:NoneType=None, sure:float=0.7, stop:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*[`parse_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#parse_board)
of the reply that comes in `chunks`. When the header says `sure` or
more, `on_step(step, k)` gets each step as soon as* its first mark is
in, and again each time its strokes change, so the first mark does not
wait for the rows of a panel or for the next step. The page adds the
strokes that it does not have yet. When the `threading.Event` `stop` is
set, it reads no more chunks and closes the stream, so the model call
ends and lets go of its backend.

`Chunked` is a test model that streams its reply in chunks of 7
characters. It writes each chunk in `events`, and the test writes each
step there too, so the order of the events shows when each step went
out.

``` python
class Chunked(Fake):
    "A `Fake` that can stream: `stream(prompt, sp)` gives its reply in chunks of 7 characters, and notes each one in `events`."
    def __init__(self, *a, **kw): super().__init__(*a, **kw); self.events = []
    def stream(self, p, sp=''):
        out = self(p, sp)
        for i in range(0, len(out), 7): self.events.append('chunk'); yield out[i:i + 7]

three = '\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [dict(op='v', n=1, sure=0.9), dict(op='step', say='Alpha bar t is the share that is left.'),
                                          dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t')), dict(op='step', say='Its root scales x0.'),
                                          dict(op='box', at='m1'), dict(op='step', say='The rest is noise.'), dict(op='underline', at='passage')])
```

Step 1 goes out before the last chunk comes, and the steps that go out
are the steps of the final board:

``` python
f = Chunked({'Tier: tutor': three})
got = []
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", on_step=lambda s, k: (got.append((k, s)), f.events.append(f'step {k}')))
ev = f.events
assert ev.index('step 1') < len(ev) - 1 - ev[::-1].index('chunk'), ev   # step 1 is before the last chunk
test_eq([dict(got)[k] for k in (1, 2, 3)], r.steps)   # the last copy of each step is the step of the board
test_eq((sorted(dict(got)), r.tier, len(f.calls)), ([1, 2, 3], 'tutor', 1))
test_eq(r.steps[0]['strokes'], [dict(op='circle', at=dict(a='m1', tex=r'\bar\alpha_t'))])
```

A tutor that is not sure sends no step. The board is the same as with a
model that cannot stream:

``` python
f, got = Chunked({'Tier: tutor': three.replace('0.9', '0.4')}), []
r = explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", web=False, on_step=lambda s, k: got.append(k))
test_eq((got, r.tier, len(r.steps)), ([], 'tutor', 3))
test_eq(r.steps, explain(Fake({'Tier: tutor': three.replace('0.9', '0.4')}), dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get alpha bar", web=False).steps)
```

A broken line in the middle drops as
[`parse_board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#parse_board)
drops it, and the next step still goes out:

``` python
lines = three.split('\n')
broken = '\n'.join(lines[:3] + ['{"op":"circle","at":"e7"}'] + lines[3:])
got = []
last = {}
b = stream_board((broken[i:i + 5] for i in range(0, len(broken), 5)), ctx, lambda s, k: last.__setitem__(k, s))
whole = parse_board(broken, ctx)
test_eq(([last[k] for k in sorted(last)], b.steps, b.dropped), (whole.steps, whole.steps, whole.dropped))
test_eq((len(last), len(b.dropped)), (3, 1))
```

When the stream breaks in step 3, after step 1 went out, the board keeps
the whole lines that came: two steps. A break before any step raises, as
a call does:

``` python
def breaks(text, at):
    yield text[:at]
    raise RuntimeError('the model stopped')
got = []
b = stream_board(breaks(three, three.index('The rest') + 3), ctx, lambda s, k: got.append(k))
test_eq((sorted(set(got)), len(b.steps)), ([1, 2], 2))
test_fail(lambda: stream_board(breaks(three, 5), ctx, lambda s, k: None), contains='the model stopped')
```

A step with a side panel goes out with its first stroke, before its rows
and before the next step. Then it goes out again as its rows come:

``` python
pan = '\n'.join(json.dumps(o) for o in [dict(op='v', n=1, sure=0.9), dict(op='step', say='Each test is a question.'), dict(op='panel', head='Make a question'),
    dict(op='row', cells=['[1.0]'], to='1.414', at='passage'), dict(op='row', cells=['[2.0]'], to='2.0'), dict(op='step', say='Then it adds up.')]) + '\n'
seen_ = []
stream_board((pan[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, len(pan), 4)), ctx, lambda s, k: seen_.append((k, len(s['strokes']))))
test_eq(seen_, [(1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 0)])
```

The stream of a test model passes the guard too: a key in the question
never reaches the model.

``` python
f = Chunked({'Tier: tutor': three})
explain(f, dict(anchors=ctx.anchors), "I don't get sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ", on_step=lambda s, k: None)
assert f.events and 'sk-test1234567890abcdefXYZ' not in f.calls[0][0] and '[SECRET]' in f.calls[0][0]
```

A set `stop` ends the read at the next chunk, and the stream closes. No
more step goes out:

``` python
import threading
```

``` python
stop, got, shut = threading.Event(), [], []
def slow():
    try:
        for i in range(0, len(three), 7):
            if i > three.index('Its root') + 30: stop.set()   # the learner stops while step 2 comes
            yield three[i:i + 7]
    finally: shut.append(True)
b = stream_board(slow(), ctx, lambda s, k: got.append(k), stop=stop)
test_eq((got, shut), ([1], [True]))
```

## The board in the page

`core/board.js` draws the checked board. It takes its numbers from
Clicky (github.com/farzaa/clicky, MIT):

- **The pointer.** A small triangle in the board ink flies to each mark
  on a quadratic arc. The arc lifts by `min(d * 0.2, 80)` px, the flight
  takes `clamp(d / 800, 0.6, 1.4)` s, and the easing is smoothstep. The
  pointer turns to its path and grows to 1.3x as it lands, then settles
  on a spring (response 0.4, damping 0.6). A mark draws from its tip.
- **The glow.** A `box` is a soft ring and halo that blooms and then
  settles. It stays 10 px outside the text, so it never cuts it.
- **The marker.** A `circle` on a formula part or on words adds a wide
  marker stroke through the glyphs. Its blend mode comes from the
  surface under it: `multiply` on a light surface, `screen` on a dark
  one. A white figure in dark mode still uses `multiply`.
- **The chips.** A
  [`label`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/ground.html#label) is
  a pastel chip with a coloured bar at its left, dark text in a sans
  font, and a thin leader line that ends in a dot on the part. Each
  label in a step has its own pastel. The chip pops in on a spring, and
  it never covers its target.
- **The strokes.** Rings, underlines and sketches are perfect-freehand
  strokes with pressure, and they draw on as a pen does. An arrow is one
  light Rough.js stroke with a filled head. Marks from earlier steps
  fade to 45 %, and the glow of an earlier step goes.
- **The side panel.** The example of Explain is a card on warm paper at
  the top right of the window, in a hand font, with the values in
  monospace. Each step adds its row: the circle on the value on the page
  at its word, the curve from it 120 ms later, the row when the curve
  lands, then each cell 80 ms after the one before. Rows stay for the
  next steps; their curves fade. A new beat (a new `panel` line) has its
  own title. While the panel shows, the page column moves left, so the
  panel never covers a mark. Below 1100 px the panel stands in the page,
  under the marked part.
- **The scroll.** Before a step draws, the page scrolls its first mark
  into view when the mark is off screen or under the strip.
- **The voice.** Each word of the spoken line in the strip lights up
  when it is said.
- **The state line.** While the guide works, the strip shows one line:
  the `wait` text of the latest state event, a chip that says *on this
  Mac* or *hosted · <company>*, the seconds after 3 s while the model
  writes, and Stop. Stop and Esc end the request, so the model stream
  closes. The caption of a board names its model, and has Voice off and
  Stop. The end shows what the guide saved, with Undo, and the hint line
  when the board counted as a hint on the open check.
- **The figure.** The picture of a figure goes to the vision model only
  when the question is about it (the learner showed it, or the question
  names it), and the line says so first: “The guide sends this figure to
  <model> to find its labels.”

With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the pointer jumps to its mark, and the
marks and chips fade in for 150 ms. Text from the model goes in with
`textContent` only.

## Host hooks: the board on another page

Leela and other hosts use the same board. `play` takes the hooks of the
page in `host`. Each hook is optional, and the defaults keep the
behaviour of abhyasa:

``` js
abhyasaBoard.play(board, {labels, fast, quiet, auto, host: {resolve, speak, demo, assets}})
```

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Option</th>
<th>What it does</th>
<th>Default</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>labels</code></td>
<td><code>{anchorId: {label: [x0, y0, x1, y1]}}</code>, the label boxes
of a figure, 0 to 1000 of the anchor</td>
<td><code>{}</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>fast</code></td>
<td>Draw each step at once, with no voice and no flight</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>quiet</code></td>
<td>No voice: the words are timed by their letters, and
<code>host.speak</code> is not called</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>auto</code></td>
<td>Go to the next step 1.2 s after the line is said</td>
<td><code>true</code> (<code>false</code> when <code>fast</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>host.resolve(id) -&gt; Element\|null</code></td>
<td>The element of anchor <code>id</code>. A formula element names its
parts in <code>data-parts</code>: JSON
<code>[[tex, elementId], ...]</code>. The board finds each part by its
id in the element, then in the document. A token with no part element
marks the whole formula</td>
<td><code>document.querySelector('[data-guide-id="&lt;id&gt;"]')</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>host.speak(text, onWord, done)</code></td>
<td>Say <code>text</code>. Call <code>onWord(k)</code> when word
<code>k</code> (from 0, split on white space) starts, and
<code>done()</code> at the end. It can return a function that stops the
speech. The board ignores calls after the step changes</td>
<td><code>speechSynthesis</code>, timed by letters when there is no
voice</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>host.demo(set)</code></td>
<td>Move the demo to <code>set</code>, as <code>{input: value}</code>. A
host demo must do its own gate check</td>
<td><code>Rupaka.set</code> on <code>[data-guide-id="demo"]</code>, only
when each gate is done, so the result never shows first</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>host.assets</code></td>
<td>The URL folder of <code>rough.js</code> and
<code>perfect-freehand.mjs</code></td>
<td><code>'/vendor/'</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A host that gets the steps one at a time (the `step` events of the guide
route) starts the board with step 1 and `streaming: true`, gives each
next step to `add(step)`, and gives the whole board to `finish(board)`
at the end. The board waits at its last step until the next one comes.
`finish` gives `false` when the steps that show are not the first steps
of the whole board: then the host plays the whole board. A host that
does not know these calls plays the whole board, as before.

``` js
abhyasaBoard.play({steps: [step1], tier: 'tutor', sources: [], streaming: true}, opts)
abhyasaBoard.add(step2)            // true, or false when no streaming board shows
abhyasaBoard.finish(board)         // true, or false: then play(board)
```

A host with a rupaka demo gets its anchors from
`abhyasaBoard.demoAnchors(host)`, so that each host uses the same ids:
`demo` for the demo, `in:<bind>` for each block whose bind is a key of
`spec.state`, and `out:<n>` for each readout, caption, bars, pixels or
plot block that shows, with n from 1 in the depth-first order of the
spec. An id of more than 40 characters is dropped, never cut. The server
never numbers these ids.
[`clean_context`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#clean_context)
only checks their shape.

`abhyasaBoard.state` gives `{i, steps, tier, first, done, streaming}`,
and `abhyasaBoard.pointer` gives `{tip, to, flying}` in window pixels.
Formula parts come from `core/texparts.js` (`window.abhyasaTex`):
`texParts`, `texAtoms`, `texWrap`, and `trust`, the one KaTeX trust
rule. A host vendors that file to mark its formulas the same way.

## Show while you talk

While the learner holds Hyper+E or types in the box, they can show the
part they mean with the mouse. `guide.js` keeps the pointer path in
memory only while the guide asks: page pixels, at most 30 points a
second, the last 15 s and 600 points. The ask takes the path, finds the
gestures, and forgets the path.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Gesture</th>
<th>Rule</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>circle</td>
<td>The path turns 300 degrees or more (and not more than 540) in 8 s,
comes back near its start (20 px, or 35 % of the loop size), and its box
is 24 px or more on each side</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>point</td>
<td>The pointer stays inside 12 px for 400 ms or more, after it came
from 40 px or more away. A rest at the end of a circle is part of the
circle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>nothing</td>
<td>A small shake of a hand on the mouse, a swipe, a zigzag, an open
arc, a small loop</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A circle selects the anchors that it covers most. A point selects the
smallest anchor that holds it. A gesture on no anchor gets the element
with text under it as a new anchor. The ask sends at most 5 items, the
latest first, as `ctx.focus`: `{kind, box, anchors, t, words}`. `box` is
from 0 to 1000 of the first anchor, `t` is in ms from the start of the
question, and `words` are the last words in the box near that time. The
Mac overlay sends the same shape, with the same rules
(`tests/data/gesture_paths.json` holds the sample paths that both test).

While the learner draws, a faint trail of the last 1.5 s shows in the
board ink, and a soft ring shows on each circle or point for 1.5 s. With
`prefers-reduced-motion`, there is no trail, and the ring does not move.
